Subject: Request: extended terms + VAT routing (Net60)

Hi Laura,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team liked the performance metrics. We're planning the Q1 rollout and want to confirm payment terms and tax routing before we commit to volumes. Two asks from procurement and finance:

1) Credit limit: we are requesting Net60 on an initial credit line of EUR 350,000 (covers expected MRR + buffer for burst traffic).
2) Tax/VAT: invoices should go to Finn Health B.V. (NL) with reverse-charge treatment where applicable — we'll provide VAT IDs for both entities.
3) Security of funds: procurement prefers either a conditional letter of credit or an escrow/holdback arrangement until the first 90 days of production.

I've attached our Q3 financials and an initial PO estimate to help with underwriting (attachment: Finn_Financials_Q3.pdf). Can Redwood outline acceptable forms of collateral and whether an early-pay swap (discount for earlier settlement) is on the table?

Would prefer a written sketch so we can run it past legal and treasury.

Best,
Emma Lowe

Emma — really appreciate the data and the clarity on entity routing. Looping in Karthik (finance) and Olga (tax) to scope the paths. Quick sketch from our side to get the conversation moving:

Option A — Early-pay swap (preferred operational path):
- Standard contract: Net60.
- For the first 3 invoices: Finn Health may elect an early-pay swap: pay within 15 days in exchange for a 1.25% invoice discount. Early-pay election is per-invoice.
- Redwood provides a forecast-backed invoice schedule (see attached Draft_Invoice_Schedule.xlsx) and a first-invoice hold for 7% as short-term credit insurance to be released after two on-time payments.

Option B — Conditional Letter of Credit (credit underwriting):
- Letter of credit (sight LC) for the initial 90-day onboarding period covering the requested EUR 350k (or a percentage we agree).
- When LC is in place, we can remove the 7% hold and keep Net60 standard. LC must be issued by a bank acceptable to Redwood finance and include standard beneficiary phrasing.

VAT & invoicing:
- Olga: is there anything we need to change to make reverse-charge on invoices to Finn Health B.V. explicit?

Next steps I recommend:
1) Emma: confirm whether Finn prefers Option A (early-pay swap + 7% release hold) or Option B (LC).
2) If Option B, provide bank contact and sample LC language.
3) If Option A, Karthik will run credit for initial release thresholds.

Happy to hop on a 30-minute call this week to finalize.

— Laura Bennett

Laura / team — thanks for the options. A couple of clarifications from treasury:

- Letter of credit: our banks are willing but issuing an LC for the full EUR 350k is expensive (fees + capital). We'd prefer a hybrid: a 10% pre-funded reserve (earmarked on our side) + Net60, with the reserve released across two subsequent invoices once service is validated.
- Early-pay swap: 1.25% is reasonable, but operationally we can't make early-pay elections per invoice at scale. Can you offer a program-level early-pay discount (e.g., 1% applied to all invoices if we commit to paying within 20 days for the first 3 months)?
- VAT: We'll confirm VAT IDs, but we need clear invoice wording: "reverse-charge — recipient liable" and a split of gross vs. VAT-exempt items.

We prefer not to open an LC unless absolutely necessary; if Redwood requires it as a hard precondition we can discuss but would need to factor the fees into TCO.

Regards,

Peter / Emma — thanks for the quick turnaround and the practical framing. Here's a concise agreement that should minimize bank fees and get you operational without a full LC: 

Agreed path (summary) — onboarding tranche (first 90 days):
1) Credit instrument: Finn Health will supply either (a) a bank-issued conditional letter of credit for 50% of the requested line (sight LC) OR (b) a 10% pre-funded reserve (earmarked by your treasury) into an escrow account managed by Redwood's payments partner. Either route removes the per-invoice 7% hold described earlier.
2) Terms & discount: Standard invoicing remains Net60. For the first 3 calendar invoices, Finn may elect a program-level early-pay arrangement: commit to paying within 20 days for all three invoices and receive a 1.0% discount applied to each. Election documented in amendment.
3) VAT / invoicing: invoices will be issued to Finn Health B.V.; wording will include "reverse-charge — recipient liable" and we will break out taxable vs. non-taxable line items. Olga will add the tax clause to the SOW appendix.
4) Release schedule: if the pre-funded reserve option is chosen, funds are released 50% after the second on-time invoice and remaining 50% after the third on-time invoice. If LC chosen, releases per bank sight terms.
5) Escalation & limits: Redwood finance (Karthik) will set an interim credit cap of EUR 400k for the first 90 days subject to delivery of invoices and KYC. After 90 days we re-evaluate to remove caps or reduce collateral.

Next steps:
- Peter / Emma: confirm which credit instrument you prefer (LC 50% or 10% reserve).
- If LC: share bank contact and proposed beneficiary language for our legal team.
- If reserve: we'll send escrow instructions and a short amendment for signature.

I've initiated a DocuSign amendment for the early-pay program/credit instrument choices (link below). Once you choose an instrument we'll finalize the onboarding schedule.
